en: be refused; be rejected; be denied

examples.en: The application gets refused.
The payment was declined.
If the password is wrong, access is denied.
It is a request the court rejected.
My card was declined. Why would that be?
To avoid being refused, submit all the documents.

explain: 기계나 제도가 받지 않았다는 사실을 말할 때 자주 써요. 카드 결제, 접속, 신청서에 많이 나와요. 사람에게 거절당한 속상함까지 담으려면 '거부당하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is common for stating that a machine or system did not accept something, such as card payments, logins and applications. To carry the hurt of being turned down by a person, use '거부당하다'.

examples.ko: 경제난으로 문을 닫는 가게가 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More shops are closing because of economic hardship.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 몇 년째 경제난을 겪고 있어요.
examples.en: That country has been going through economic difficulties for years.
As the economic hardship dragged on, people cut back on spending.
Even amid economic hardship, many people donate.

examples.ko: 심한 경제난에 시달리는 가정을 돕는 행사예요.
examples.en: It is an event to help families suffering from severe economic hardship.
Economic hardship is not solved overnight.

explain: 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 말로, 보통 나라, 회사, 가계가 돈 때문에 어려운 상황에 써요. '-난'은 '어려움'이라서 '구인난', '주택난'처럼 같은 짜임의 말이 많아요. 내 지갑 사정은 '돈이 없어서 힘들어요'처럼 일상적으로 말해요.
explain_en: It is common in the news and usually describes a country, company or household in money trouble. '-난' means difficulty, so there are many words built the same way, like '구인난' and '주택난'. For your own wallet, people say something plain like '돈이 없어서 힘들어요'.

examples.en: The police blocked the protesters' march.
The defender stops the opposing player's attack.
Everyone worked hard to stop the crime.

examples.ko: 몰래 들어오는 사람을 저지할 수 없었어요.
examples.en: We couldn't stop the person sneaking in.
The residents are blocking the development.
If we keep opposing it to the end, the plan might change.

explain: 저지하다는 어떤 일이 일어나지 못하게 막는 거예요. '막다'보다 격식 있는 말이라 뉴스와 스포츠 해설에 자주 나와요. 사람이나 행동을 막는 데 쓰고, 문이나 길을 물리적으로 닫는 것에는 보통 '막다'를 써요.
explain_en: 저지하다 is to stop something from happening. It is more formal than '막다' and often appears in the news and sports commentary. It is used for stopping people or actions; for physically blocking a door or road, plain '막다' is usual.

examples.ko: 여름마다 전력난 때문에 에어컨 사용을 줄이자는 말이 나와요.
examples.en: Every summer people say we should use air conditioners less because of power shortages.
When power shortages get severe, running factories becomes hard.

examples.ko: 정부는 전력난을 막으려고 절전 캠페인을 시작했어요.
examples.en: The government started a power-saving campaign to prevent a power shortage.

examples.ko: 이 나라는 전력난으로 하루에 몇 시간씩 불이 꺼져요.
examples.en: In this country the lights go out for several hours a day because of power shortages.

examples.ko: 전력난에 대비해서 건물마다 불을 끄고 있어요.
examples.en: Every building is turning off lights to prepare for a power shortage.

examples.ko: 전력난은 에어컨과 난방을 많이 쓰는 철에 더 커져요.
examples.en: Power shortages grow worse in seasons when air conditioning and heating are heavily used.

explain: '-난'은 '구인난', '주택난', '재정난'처럼 모자라서 생기는 어려움을 나타내요. 전력난은 전기가 부족한 상황을 뉴스에서 말할 때 쓰고, 일상에서는 '전기가 부족하다'라고 해요. 발음은 [절력난]이에요.
explain_en: The ending '-난' marks difficulty caused by a shortage, as in '구인난', '주택난' and '재정난'. 전력난 is used in the news for a lack of electricity, while daily talk says '전기가 부족하다'. It is pronounced [절력난].

examples.en: Yesterday that person was singled out as the culprit.
I was flustered when the teacher suddenly called on me.

examples.ko: 이 문제는 가장 큰 원인으로 지목돼요.
examples.en: This problem is named as the biggest cause.
The student who was called on, please come to the front.
The team that was picked as a title favorite lost.
If you are picked as the next presenter, you have to answer.

explain: '지목하다'는 누군가를 콕 집어 말하는 쪽이고, '지목되다'는 그렇게 집힌 쪽이에요. 수업에서는 선생님이 학생을, 뉴스에서는 사람들이 범인·원인·후보를 지목해요. 안 좋은 일의 범인이나 원인에 많이 쓰이지만 우승 후보에도 써요.
explain_en: '지목하다' is the side that singles someone out, and 'jimokdoeda' is the side that gets singled out. In class a teacher calls on a student; in the news people name a culprit, cause, or candidate. It is often used for culprits and causes of bad things, but also for title favorites.

examples.en: The job shortage among young people is really serious these days.

examples.ko: 취직난 때문에 졸업을 미루는 학생이 많아요.
examples.en: Many students put off graduating because of the job shortage.
When the economy gets worse, the job shortage gets worse too.
The news keeps talking about the job shortage.

examples.ko: 취직난을 해결하려면 일자리가 더 늘어야 해요.
examples.en: To solve the job shortage, there need to be more jobs.

examples.ko: 이 나라는 오래전부터 취직난에 시달리고 있어요.
examples.en: This country has suffered from a job shortage for a long time.

explain: '취업난'도 거의 같은 뜻으로 써요. 보통 '취직난이 심하다/심각하다', '취직난에 시달리다'처럼 말해요. 반대로 일할 사람을 구하기 어려운 상황은 '구인난'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '취업난' is used with almost the same meaning. People usually say '취직난이 심하다/심각하다' or '취직난에 시달리다'. The opposite situation, where employers cannot find workers, is called '구인난'.

examples.en: Rainwater seeped into the wall.

examples.ko: 추위가 옷 안까지 침투해서 몸이 떨렸어요.
examples.en: The cold got through my clothes, and I shivered.

examples.ko: 이 크림은 피부 깊이 침투하는 것 같아요.
examples.en: This cream seems to soak deep into the skin.

examples.ko: 세균이 몸에 침투하면 열이 날 수 있어요.
examples.en: If germs get into your body, you can get a fever.

examples.ko: 특수부대가 내일 밤 기지에 침투할 거예요.
examples.en: The special forces will infiltrate the base tomorrow night.

examples.ko: 물이 침투하지 못하게 막아 주는 옷이에요.
examples.en: These are clothes that keep water from getting through.

explain: 물, 냄새, 세균처럼 스며드는 것에도, 군인이나 스파이가 몰래 들어가는 일에도 써요. 일상에서는 '스며들다'가 더 부드럽고 자주 들려요. '~에 침투하다'처럼 조사 '에'와 같이 써요.
explain_en: It fits things that seep in, like water, smells or germs, and also soldiers or spies slipping in secretly. In daily talk '스며들다' sounds softer and is more common. Use it with the particle '에', as in '~에 침투하다'.

examples.en: Many people fell victim to the accident.

examples.ko: 작은 가게들이 개발 때문에 희생되고 있어요.
examples.en: Small shops are being sacrificed because of development.
We remember the people who were lost in the war.

examples.ko: 아이들이 희생되지 않도록 안전을 지켜야 해요.
examples.en: We must keep things safe so children aren't harmed.

examples.ko: 나쁜 결정 때문에 다른 사람이 희생돼서는 안 돼요.
examples.en: Others must not be sacrificed because of a bad decision.
When someone is lost, we all grieve.

explain: '희생하다'는 자기가 일부러 내놓는 것이고, '희생되다'는 어쩔 수 없이 피해를 입거나 목숨을 잃는 것이에요. 사고, 전쟁, 재난 뉴스에서 '희생자'와 같이 나와요. 가볍게 쓰지 않는 말이에요.
explain_en: '희생하다' is giving something up on purpose, while '희생되다' is suffering harm or losing one's life against one's will. It appears with '희생자' (victim) in news about accidents, war, and disasters. It is not used lightly.
